correctness.rationale: Commuting with the permutation unit is equivalent to invariance under its simultaneous relabeling of both rows. A two-vertex block gives an equivariant partner involution, so each vertex cycle is either isolated, matched internally by the unique antipodal pairing when even, or matched bijectively to a second cycle of the same length with ℓ shifts. A cross-row match contributes ℓ to rank. For each length and each k, choose k top and k bottom cycles, then match them in k!ℓ^k ways; the remaining two sets of m−k cycles have independent same-row matching counts. This yields the factor in (1) and positivity for all and only the indicated k choices. Taking all cycles transversal gives z_sigma. For rank deficit exactly ℓ in a single length factor there are m²(m−1)!ℓ^(m−1)s_ell² choices: choose the two unused cycles and their internal states and match the rest transversally. After reversal and normalization this gives first coefficient m s_ell²/ℓ. The degree and leading coefficient of C give n and z_sigma; formally dividing out every previously recovered shorter-length factor isolates this first coefficient in degree ℓ, since longer-length factors start later. This proves recovery including absent lengths. Rank-wise Burnside with class sizes n!/z_lambda proves (4); a hand check at n=3 gives 5+8u+4u²+3u³. Finite reported tests were not rerun and do not justify the general theorem by themselves.
residual_risks: The exponential extraction is interpreted in formal power series in x,y over rational polynomials in u, not as a finite polynomial before extraction.
This argument needs a permutation unit; it is not a centralizer formula for arbitrary diagrams.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Rook-Brauer and partial Brauer terminology can refer to the same diagram family; the distinction here is the subset counted, not the name. Independent top and bottom matchings and arbitrary cross-row shifts are not encoded by the mirrored character fixed set. At u=1 one may forget row types and count invariant partial matchings for the doubled permutation, but that does not preserve transversal rank.

originality.rationale: The supported distinct claim is the full two-row transversal-rank fixed-diagram polynomial together with complete reconstruction of cycle type. The most relevant character formulas already use matching of equal-length cycles and the same even/odd factor, but for a different fixed set. The diagram definition, standard matching enumeration and Burnside averaging are not themselves novelty claims.
residual_risks: An unlocated colored involution cycle index or all-diagram fixed-matching theorem could encode (1); no historical priority is certified. Any such formula would also have to be checked for the complete reconstruction consequence.
Chronology is unresolved for the distinct same-day nilpotent analogue.

value.rationale: For a natural diagram monoid, recording transversal rank instead of a single centralizer order gives a computable invariant that separates all permutation cycle types. The reversible deficit calculation explains exactly where the missing cycle data appear, including lengths occurring once, and the same polynomial yields exact rank-wise orbit counts. That is more than a table recomputation or an application of Burnside alone.
residual_risks: Value is limited to permutation-unit centralizers and transversal rank; the finding gives no general semigroup-conjugacy classification.
